evidence: Independent STS pair-coverage checks gave block counts 7,12,26,35,57 with every pair covered once.
Independent sail enumeration by 4-block degree-profile/center-transversal characterization reproduced 28,72,260,420,912.
Independent DPLL search found sail-free colourings for 7,9,13,15 and proved UNSAT for the 57-variable, 912-sail named cyclic STS(19) instance.
The repository tree on main equals the assigned tree SHA.
correctness.summary: Independent reconstruction verified the five named Steiner triple systems, sail counts 28/72/260/420/912, existence of sail-free 2-colourings for orders 7,9,13,15, and UNSAT of the sail-free NAE instance for the named cyclic STS(19).

originality.summary: Prior literature located the sail as the remaining <=4-block case and posed sail t-Ramsey as open, but the audit did not locate an antecedent for this exact named-system finite certificate. This is evidence of a specific finite contribution, not a proof of global novelty.

scientific_value.summary: The exact witnesses and UNSAT benchmark are useful finite evidence and reproducibility targets, while the record correctly limits itself to named systems and does not resolve the general sail-Ramsey problem.

limitations: No claim of exhaustive novelty search is made.
The result does not prove that every STS(19), or all sufficiently large STS, is sail-Ramsey.
